verses.133:1a: {ecce}, bendizei {dominum}, * todos os servos do Senhor:
verses.133:1b: {quistatis} na casa do Senhor, * {atriis} da casa do nosso Deus.

decisions.why: ecce + imperative is a Hebraism through the Greek (ἰδοὺ δή). Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT drop ecce and turn nunc into a connective ('Agora, pois'); DRB keeps both words ('Behold now bless ye'). At Compline the nunc is heard as the hour itself, beside 'In nóctibus'.

options.label: Eis agora
options.note: Draft. Both Latin words, in the Latin's order; 'eis' is the standing Portuguese for ecce and needs no footnote.

options.label: Agora, pois
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Smooth, but ecce goes unheard and 'pois' makes an inference the Latin does not make.

options.label: Vede, agora
options.note: Turns the particle into a verb, as 'Behold' does; it then piles two imperatives ('Vede… bendizei') where the Latin has one.

decisions.why: The psalter has benedícere with the accusative (here, 15:7, 33:2) and with the dative (102:20–22 Benedícite Dómino, 134:19–20, 67:27, 113:26 — checked in the DO Latin). Portuguese can keep the difference for nothing: direct object for the accusative, 'ao Senhor' for the dative.

options.label: o Senhor
options.note: Draft, with pt-PT. The accusative as a direct object; leaves 'ao Senhor' for the psalms that have Dómino.

options.label: ao Senhor
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 ('bendizei ao Senhor'): the devotional habit of the preposition before God's name. Good Portuguese; it only gives up the Latin's two constructions.

decisions.why: stare is to stand, and the Greek is ἑστῶτες, 'standing' (DRB 'Who stand'): the servants are on their feet, ministering, at night. pt-PT flattens it to 'estais'; Matos Soares has the old 'assistis'. The identical verse is 134:2, and 121:2 has 'Stantes erant pedes nostri in átriis tuis', where the standing cannot be lost. The verse also opens on a relative that hangs from the vocative of 133:1a, and the two halves of a choir say them in turn.

options.label: Que estais de pé
options.note: Draft. The concrete posture kept (rule 5). Opening the verse on 'Que', dependent on the verse before, is what the Latin does (Qui statis) and what Dom Marcos does in the Diurnal ('Que permaneceis na casa do Senhor').

options.label: Vós que estais de pé
options.note: Names the subject (allowed by rule 2) so that the verse can stand alone when the other side of the choir takes it; one syllable more (+3 on the Latin by checks.py).

options.label: Vós que estais
options.note: pt-PT. The smoothest, and 'estar' is stare's own child; but the standing is lost.

decisions.why: The ambiguity reader listed 'átrios' among the words a churchgoer may not know. átrium (αὐλή) is the court of the Temple, and the word recurs in the psalter (28:2, 64:5, 83:2, 83:11, 91:14, 95:8, 99:3b, 115:9, 121:2, 134:2 — grep in the DO Latin), so whatever stands here stands there.

options.label: nos átrios
options.note: Draft, kept, with Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. The Latin's word, still used of the forecourt of a church; 'casa do Senhor' on either side of it tells the hearer what kind of thing it is.

options.label: nos pátios
options.note: Offered because of the ambiguity reader's flag: a word everyone knows, and the same thing; but it is heard of a school or a house, never of a church.

decisions.why: A plural (LXX ἐν ταῖς νυξίν; DRB 'In the nights'), and the word that makes this a psalm of Compline. The stylist's one remark on the psalm: 'Nas noites', with nothing saying which nights, sounds traced from the Latin and the mouth expects a continuation.

options.label: Durante as noites
options.note: Draft 2, from the stylist — and it is Matos Soares 1932's own rendering. The plural and the word stay; only the preposition yields to the ear (rule 2). Cost: the first colon is now 19 syllables by checks.py against the Latin's 15 (about 17 in the mouth, with 'Durante‿as' and 'para‿o').

options.label: Nas noites
options.note: Draft 1. 'In nóctibus' word for word and the right length; heard as unfinished ('nas noites de…?').

options.label: De noite
options.note: pt-PT. The most natural and the shortest; the plural — night after night — is lost.

decisions.why: The psalter lifts hands, eyes and souls with several verbs — leváre (120:1, 122:1), extóllere (here; 27:2 dum extóllo manus meas; 74:6), eleváre (140:2), exaltáre — and they should not all become one Portuguese verb. extóllere is 'to lift out or up, to raise up' (L&S).

options.label: erguei
options.note: Draft, from the Diurnal Monástico 1962 ('Erguei vossas mãos'). Leaves 'levantar' free for leváre and 'elevar' for eleváre. The vós imperative is safe: 'erguei' is not 'ergui'.

options.label: levantai
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT. Just as plain; but it is the natural word for leváre ('Levávi óculos meos'), and it is one vowel from the past 'levantei'.

options.label: elevai
options.note: A little more solemn; it is the cognate of another verb of the psalter, eleváre (140:2 elevátio mánuum meárum).

decisions.why: A neuter plural adjective used as a noun, after the Greek εἰς τὰ ἅγια: 'toward the holy (places)', that is, the sanctuary. DRB 'to the holy places'; Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT 'para o santuário'. The psalter also has the noun sanctuárium (72:17, 73:7, 82:13, 88:40) and the singular 'in sancto' (21:4, 59:8, 62:3, 76:14, 150:1 in sanctis), so the choice here touches those places.

options.label: para o lugar santo
options.note: Draft, kept. Keeps sanctus audible and keeps sancta apart from sanctuárium → santuário. The Greek plural names one place, so the singular — as both Vulgate translators in the parallels have it. The ambiguity reader heard it either as a holy part of the temple or as heaven, God's dwelling: no wider than 'in sancta'.

options.label: para o santuário
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT (the Diurnal too: 'na direção do santuário'). What the phrase means, in one word; it merges sancta with sanctuárium.

options.label: para os lugares santos
options.note: The Latinist's one remark (minor): sancta is a plural and the singular does not keep its number; so DRB ('holy places'). Refused as the text: the remark is right about the grammar, but in Brazil 'os lugares santos' are the pilgrimage sites of the Holy Land, so the plural would say something the Latin does not; and Matos Soares 1932, the limit set by rule 2, has a singular. The Latinist raised the same point again on draft 2, this time as 'major' (critic/v2.latinist.json): the gate is therefore not clean on this one word, and the choice is Gustavo's — if number outweighs connotation, this option becomes the text.

decisions.why: The whole psalm turns on one verb said three times: benedícite… benedícite… Benedícat — bless the Lord, and the Lord bless you. Portuguese has two verbs, bendizer (to speak well of, to bless God) and abençoar (to give a blessing), and every parallel splits them here (MS1932, pt-PT, Diurnal: 'abençoe'). Rule 2 forbids dropping a repetition the Latin has; but 'abençoar' is what any Brazilian says. benedícere with God as subject recurs (66:7–8 Benedícat nos Deus, 127:5 Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion), so this wants a ruling.

options.label: te bendiga
options.note: Draft. One verb, as in the Latin: bendizei… bendizei… bendiga. 'Bendizer' with God as subject is dictionary Portuguese ('Deus te bendiga'), a little old-fashioned, understood at once. The blind readers bear this out: the stylist, unprompted, named 133:3 the best line of the psalm ('a bênção final corre com naturalidade'), and the ambiguity reader paraphrased it as 'Que o Senhor envie de Sião a bênção para ti' without hesitating over the verb.

options.label: te abençoe
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT, Diurnal Monástico 1962. The everyday word for what God does; the psalm's hinge — the same verb going up and coming down — is no longer heard.

decisions.latin: Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
decisions.why: In natural Portuguese order the relative lands next to 'Sião' ('de Sião, que fez o céu e a terra'), and Sion would seem to have made heaven and earth. The Latin's masculine 'qui' cannot mislead. 'qui fecit cælum et terram' is a formula (113:23, 120:2, 123:8, 145:6), so the words 'que fez o céu e a terra' should stay fixed whatever is done around them.

options.label: O Senhor te bendiga de Sião, * ele que fez…

forms.v3: O Senhor {benedicat} de Sião, * ele que fez o céu e a terra.

options.note: Draft. Natural order, and the subject named again at the mediant — DRB 'he that made', and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 'Êle que fêz o céu e a terra', from which the 'ele' is taken. The formula itself is untouched.

options.label: Bendiga-te de Sião o Senhor, * que fez…

forms.v3: {benedicat_encl} de Sião o Senhor, * que fez o céu e a terra.

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and pt-PT: verb first, as in the Latin, and 'o Senhor' moved to the mediant so that the relative finds it. Nothing supplied; but it is an inversion nobody would say, in a verse said every night.

choices.133:1a: benedícite → bendizei (safe at the vós imperative: the past is 'bendisse'). 'Senhor' closes both cola, and the first colon of 133:1b too: the Latin does the same (Dóminum / Dómini / Dómini). 'omnes servi Dómini' is a vocative; no 'vós' or 'ó' is supplied (Matos Soares adds 'vós', the Diurnal 'ó'). servus → servo, as in the Nunc dimittis (servum tuum).
choices.133:1b: The verse hangs from the vocative of 133:1a, as in the Latin. 134:2 is the same verse word for word (checked in the DO Latin): whoever translates Ps 134 copies this one. 'átrios' kept (átrium; the courts of the Temple): a word still used of churches. 'domus' → casa both times. The ambiguity reader heard 'a casa do Senhor' as the church where the hearers are — which is how the verse is prayed. The Hebrew has no second colon here and puts 'in the nights' in this verse; the Latin follows the LXX and so does the translation.
choices.133:2: 'In nóctibus' is plural (LXX ἐν ταῖς νυξίν; DRB 'In the nights') and stays plural; draft 2 has 'Durante as noites' for draft 1's 'Nas noites' (see the decision). First colon +4 by checks.py, accepted: nothing in it is added, and the two elisions bring it to about 17 in the mouth. Second colon −2, within range.
choices.133:3: The psalm turns from the plural servants (vós) to a singular 'te': 'te', with tu-forms nowhere else needed. The ambiguity reader heard the 'te' as each hearer singly, a particular person, or the community as one — the Latin's 'te' is as open, and nothing is done about it. It also listed 'Sião' as a word a hearer may not know: a proper name, kept. 'ex Sion' → 'de Sião' (MS1932, pt-PT, Diurnal); 'desde Sião' would mark the origin more plainly but is heavier. 127:5 has the same blessing with the dative (Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion) and should follow whatever is ruled here.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm133.txt. The project reports that it was collated against the printed Hetzenauer 1914 Clementine (pp. 557–558) with no divergence of wording; I did not re-read the page.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps133.md. Bolls files this psalm's Douay-Rheims as Ps 135 and parallels.py found it (the text shown is the right psalm). The Latin follows the LXX against the Hebrew in 133:1b (the second colon, 'in átriis domus Dei nostri', is not in the Hebrew) and in placing 'In nóctibus' at the head of 133:2. Occurrences quoted in the decisions (benedícere + accusative / dative, extóllere, sanctuárium / in sancto, qui fecit cælum et terram, ex Sion) were checked with grep in the DO Latin psalter, not recalled. Address: vós for the servants, tu for the 'te' of 133:3.

Draft 1: hard pass. No length or cadence flags. One rhyme flag, 133:1a (Senhor / Senhor at mediant and final): accepted, because it is the Latin's own repetition at the same places (Dóminum / Dómini).

Draft 1. One remark, minor: 133:2 'in sancta' is a neuter plural and 'o lugar santo' does not keep the number → 'para os lugares santos'. Refused as the text, kept as an option, for the reason given in the decision ('os lugares santos' names the Holy Land sites in Brazil; MS1932 and pt-PT have a singular). Everything else confirmed, the marks included.

Draft 1. One remark: 133:2 'Nas noites' sounds traced from the Latin → 'Durante as noites'. Taken: the plural and the word stay, and it is Matos Soares 1932's rendering. Best line 133:3 (which has 'te bendiga'), worst 133:2; no accidental rhyme heard, every cadence sound.

Draft 1, Portuguese only. Five items, all the Latin's own openness heard correctly (who the servants are, which house, 'o lugar santo' as temple or heaven, who 'te' is, 'de Sião'). 'O Senhor te bendiga' was understood as a blessing without remark. Unknown words: 'átrios' (decision added, word kept) and 'Sião' (a proper name, kept).
v2: 133:2 'Nas noites' → 'Durante as noites'. New decisions: atriis, innoctibus. Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the v1 critics read).
Draft 2: hard pass. 133:2 first colon +4 (19 against the Latin's 15), accepted: nothing is added, and 'Durante‿as' and 'para‿o' run together in the mouth. Rhyme flag in 133:1a as before.

Draft 2. The same single remark on 'in sancta', now rated major; nothing on 'Durante as noites' or anywhere else. Still refused as the text, for the same reason, and left to Gustavo as the one open point of the gate — the option is ready in the 'insancta' decision.
